plan.title: Treatment x time interaction in 12-sample bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is explicitly an interaction question: does the treatment effect at t1 differ from the treatment effect at t0? The data are gene-level Salmon counts (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples) with a metadata table (metadata.csv, 12 rows: condition, time, time_hours) describing a balanced 2 conditions x 2 time points x 3 replicates design in a single batch, human cell line. A balanced full-factorial design with a single batch means the interaction term is directly estimable and no batch covariate is needed.

The backbone is therefore a single DESeq2 model with ~ condition + time + condition:time (T1S1), from which three contrasts are extracted: the simple treatment effect at t0, the simple treatment effect at t1, and the interaction (difference of differences) which is the literal answer to the question. Anticipating the two main statistical hazards: (a) n=3 per cell gives 8 residual degrees of freedom for the interaction — the interaction test is roughly half as powerful as either simple effect, so absence of significant interaction genes must be reported as 'not detected at this power', never as 'no time-dependence'; (b) the counts are Salmon gene-level output and the profile does not record whether a length/abundance correction was applied, so T1S1 must check integrality and round rather than assume, and must not apply a second length correction.

T1S0 handles the design bookkeeping and QC that the model depends on and that would otherwise be silently assumed: sample-name concordance between the two CSVs, confirmation that the 12 samples really are 3 per condition x time cell, low-count filtering, VST + PCA to see whether time or condition dominates the variance and whether any replicate is an outlier. T1S2 then quantifies the interaction beyond per-gene significance — correlation and scatter of the two simple-effect log2 fold changes, counts of genes by concordance class (treatment-responsive at t0 only, t1 only, both same direction, both opposite direction), which answers 'does the effect differ' as a global summary even when few individual genes clear FDR on the interaction term.

T2S1 gives the biological reading: fgsea on the hallmark and GO-BP human gene sets (both staged under /mnt/refs) run separately on the t0, t1, and interaction rankings, so a shift in which programmes move between time points is visible at the pathway level, where power is higher than at the gene level. It is scoped as enrichment on ranked gene lists, so it runs whatever the gene-level interaction yields; if the gene identifiers in counts.csv are not HGNC symbols it must map them via the staged UniProt human ID mapping and report the mapping rate.
